top_stories.title: Some USCIS officers ask green card applicants why they bypassed consular processing… - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **USCIS** officers are beginning to question green-card applicants about their decision to pursue Adjustment of Status (AOS) rather than consular processing abroad, following a controversial May 22 policy memo. While some field officers are questioning applicants and others are approving cases without reference to the memo, **USCIS** is still awaiting further guidance on the policy.  Immigration attorneys advise applicants to prepare comprehensive evidence files that highlight positive factors such as employment history, tax compliance, and community ties.

top_stories.title: UK brothers convicted of 1984 murder after more than 40-year cold case solved by family confessions | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Michael** and **Anthony Stewart**, two UK brothers, were found guilty of the 1984 murder of **Anthony Littler**, a London civil servant. The case had remained unsolved for over four decades before detectives reopened the investigation in 2022, uncovering family confessions and fresh evidence.  A breakthrough came when their younger brother, **Daniel Stewart**, provided information about his brothers' involvement in the attack. The investigation was further strengthened by testimony from Michael Stewart's former girlfriend, who claimed he confessed to the killing. Detectives also revisited evidence from the original inquiry, including transport records and witness statements. A postmortem examination revealed that Littler had suffered two skull fractures and a catastrophic brain injury. **Detective Chief Inspector Neil John** stated that Littler was targeted because he was alone and defenceless. The brothers are due to be sentenced in July.

top_stories.title: PoK activist Amjad Ayub Mirza calls on PM Modi to intervene over 'rights violations' in Gilgit-Baltistan - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Amjad Ayub Mirza**, a human rights activist in **Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK)**, has appealed to **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for intervention regarding widespread rights violations and growing pressure on political activists in the region. **Mirza** alleges that Pakistani security agencies are preparing a crackdown on the **Joint Awami Action Committee** ahead of a planned general strike, citing economic and humanitarian concerns as contributing factors to public discontent. He urged **Modi** to highlight the situation and support efforts for civil liberties, democratic rights, and economic justice in PoK and Gilgit-Baltistan.

top_stories.title: Down the Rabbit Hole: Why AI means 'actually Indians' for Silicon Valley in 2026 | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: Recent events have highlighted the success of Indian-American CEOs in Silicon Valley, particularly Sanjay Mehrotra, Satya Nadella, and Sundar Pichai. These leaders, who all possess engineering backgrounds, have navigated the complexities of technology companies while demonstrating a deep understanding of their products and infrastructure. They are not typical "Founder Mode" figures but rather "Operator Mode" leaders, adept at translating technical expertise into practical solutions for large-scale businesses. Their success is attributed to their ability to manage complex systems, navigate regulatory landscapes, and adapt to the evolving demands of AI.  The rise of these Indian-American CEOs reflects a shift in Silicon Valley's leadership dynamic, where competence and operational excellence are valued over charisma or grand visions.

top_stories.title: Indian man Lubana Singh added to list of 'Worst of Worst' criminals in US for narcotics dealing - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Department of Homeland Security** added 5,000 new individuals to its "Worst of the Worst" list, bringing the total number to over 35,000. The list includes individuals arrested for a range of crimes including homicide, sex offenses against children, and drug trafficking. Acting Assistant Secretary **Lauren Bis** stated that the website aims to increase transparency by allowing the public to search through criminal histories of those arrested by **ICE**.

top_stories.title: Donald Trump names William Pulte as interim spy chief ahead of Tulsi Gabbard's departure - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **President Donald Trump** appointed **William J Pulte**, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), as interim Director of National Intelligence (DNI).  Pulte will continue to hold his positions at the FHFA, Freddie Mac, and Fannie Mae while serving as caretaker DNI. **Tulsi Gabbard**, who served as DNI since February 2025, announced her departure on May 23rd to care for her husband, who has been diagnosed with an "extremely rare form of bone cancer."

top_stories.title: Who was Henry Nowak? 18-year-old UK student killed in Southampton stabbing | World News - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Vickrum Digwa**, 23, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 21 years for the murder of **Henry Nowak**, an 18-year-old British-Polish student.  A jury found Digwa guilty of murder and possessing a knife in public after rejecting his self-defense claim. **Kiran Kaur**, Digwa's mother, was also convicted of assisting an offender. The attack occurred on Belmont Road in Southampton's Portswood area shortly before 11:30 p.m. on December 3, 2025.

top_stories.title: 'If I were 25 again...': Indian-American CEO says he would not have come to US - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Srini Madala**, an Indian-American CEO who founded three startups, believes he would not have immigrated to the US today.  He made his comments to the **San Francisco Chronicle** in response to a report exploring how the American Dream is evolving for Silicon Valley's Indian-American entrepreneurs.  Madala, who came to the US after obtaining degrees from India and attending Stanford Graduate School of Business, now serves as Chairman of the Board for the SoftSol group of companies. He has also been involved in philanthropy both in the US and India, including founding a development center in his home country.

top_stories.title: NHPC shares tumble 5% as govt’s OFS worth up to Rs 4,300 crore opens at 8% discount. Check details - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **NHPC**, the government-owned hydropower company, announced plans to sell up to 60.27 crore shares (6% equity) as part of an offer for sale (OFS). The government aims to raise more than Rs 4,279 crore from the offering, which will be conducted through a separate window mechanism on BSE and the National Stock Exchange in accordance with Securities and Exchange Board of India guidelines. **NHPC**'s OFS follows a similar move by the government divesting some stake in Coal India.  The stock has experienced declines in recent months, but remains profitable over longer timeframes.

top_stories.title: Trump names housing finance chief Bill Pulte as nation's top spy boss to replace Tulsi Gabbard
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** appointed **Bill Pulte**, the grandson of the founder of homebuilding giant PulteGroup, as acting Director of National Intelligence (DNI).  Pulte will continue serving as Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) director and chairman of mortgage finance giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac while taking on the intelligence role. The appointment comes amid ongoing tensions with **Iran** and has drawn scrutiny due to Pulte's limited intelligence background and close alignment with Trump's political agenda.  The decision replaces former congresswoman **Tulsi Gabbard**, who stepped down last month.
